summary.text: Mike Rogers is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Alabama's 3rd Congressional District, first elected in 2002. A Calhoun County attorney and small-business owner, he served on the Calhoun County Commission and in the Alabama House of Representatives, including as minority leader, before entering Congress. He chairs the House Committee on Armed Services in the 119th Congress and is seeking another term.

paragraphs.text: Born in Hammond, Indiana, in 1958. His official biography describes him as a sixth-generation East Alabamian who grew up in the mill village of Blue Mountain in Calhoun County, where his mother worked in a textile mill and his father was a firefighter.

Graduated from Saks High School, then earned bachelor's (political science, 1981) and Master of Public Administration (1984) degrees from Jacksonville State University and a J.D. from the Birmingham School of Law (1991), where his official biography says he graduated with honors.
Was previously a practicing attorney and small-business owner in Calhoun County, according to his official biography.
Served on the Calhoun County Commission from 1987 to 1990; at age 28 he was the youngest person to join it, according to Wikipedia.
Served in the Alabama House of Representatives from 1994 to 2002, as minority leader from 1998 to 2000.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2002 to succeed Bob Riley, who was elected governor; he defeated Democrat Joe Turnham 50% to 48%, according to Wikipedia.
Chairs the House Armed Services Committee, and served as ranking member of the Committee on Homeland Security in the 116th Congress, according to his official biography.

His official biography says that while on Armed Services he initiated and oversaw the creation of the U.S. Space Force, and that his district is home to the Anniston Army Depot and the Fort Benning community. Wikipedia reports that a 2017 Space Corps proposal he worked on with Rep. Jim Cooper passed the House but not the Senate, and that similar language was enacted two years later.
According to his official biography, he is married to his wife Beth and is the father of three.
